purpose: keep running systems patched against known vulnerabilities within agreed timeframes, without breaking service
entry_criteria: Inventory of systems and software versions exists
Patch policy sets timeframes by severity
Maintenance windows and rollback options exist
procedure: Match the inventory against advisories and rank by severity, exposure and exploit activity.
Test patches on a representative non-production system and record problems.
Schedule rollout in stages, starting with low-risk systems, with a rollback for each.
Apply patches by automation and verify the version and service health afterward.
Track compliance against the policy timeframes and report exceptions with owner and expiry.
Update the inventory and record what was patched.
acceptance_criteria: Critical patches are applied within the policy time or excepted
validation_method: System owner approval of the plan and exceptions.

validation.command: apt list --upgradable 2>/dev/null | head   # example for Debian systems
validation.expect: no pending security updates after rollout

validation.check: compare patched versions with the advisory's fixed versions
validation.expect: versions equal or exceed the fix

failure_modes.response: Test first, then roll out in stages

worked_example: ILLUSTRATIVE: A critical kernel advisory is tested on one staging node, rolled out to production nodes in three batches with health checks, and the compliance report shows all nodes patched within the 14-day policy.
